chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who purchased a pregnant bondwoman whose pregnancy had become evident, and then had relations with her. He said: “What he did was evil.”

So I said: “What do you say regarding her?” He said: “Did he practice withdrawal from her or not?” I said: “Answer me regarding both cases.” So he said: “If he practiced withdrawal from her, then let him have taqwa of Allah and not return to it. But if he did not practice withdrawal from her, then he must not sell that child, nor make him an inheritor; rather, he should emancipate him and assign for him something from his wealth by which he may live, for he has nourished him with his sperm.”

key_terms.الْوَلَدَ: the child born in this circumstance
key_terms.فَوَطِئَهَا: he had sexual intercourse with her
key_terms.يُعْتِقُهُ: to emancipate or set him free
key_terms.يُوَرِّثُهُ: to treat him as an inheriting heir

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man who has intercourse with a purchased pregnant bondwoman?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man who has intercourse with a bondwoman already pregnant at the time of purchase. The Imam عليه السلام condemns the act and distinguishes between the case of withdrawal and non-withdrawal, prescribing financial care and emancipation of the child in the latter case.
